title: Fixed Continuous Spatial Loop Bead Route
description: One newly authored complete static tabletop wire-and-bead toy. A single closed solid wire starts inside one base collar, follows a low straight loading run, travels through an entire pitched vertical loop, crosses a low bridge, passes through a second vertical loop in a perpendicular plane and returns into the second base collar. Five whole thick barrel-shaped beads have genuine polygonal through-bores on actual straight portions of that same route. Each bead has a small explicit eccentric offset giving matching wire/bore facet contact, rather than a floating ring. One full finite wooden base supports both terminal roots. Unlike the existing upright abacus, there are no five separate parallel straight shafts or two tall end stiles; unlike the gimballed board maze, there is no floor route, wall labyrinth or tilting tray. All whole geometry independently authored, not a bent copy of an old rod or changed bead-count asset. Three opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres, Z up and whole horizontally bounds-centred ground origin. One whole prop, zero scenes; beads and loops are not separate assets. Static illustrative pose only: no runtime slider, traversal of curves, solved motion or collision-free travel, educational outcome, child fit, choking/material suitability, load, manufacture or toy-safety claim.
